source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 9 (2022), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.210
purpose: Boundaries for reading the material candidates and the reused old judgment. Descriptive only: no assumption added, removed or exchanged; no independent correctness judgment.
reference_convention: Results are cited by their number on the shared theorem counter, whose Section-1 alignment is anchored by the old record's 'Corollary 1.8'. Displays and labels are cited by label name and 1-based source line rather than by printed equation number, because equation numbers were not cross-checked against reader.pdf.

necessary_conditions.condition: Positive depth and subcritical (fluvial) regime, uniformly in time
necessary_conditions.source_lines: 266-280; display label fluvial0 at 271-277; displays label Hinfty and label fluvial at 343-348; display at 1107
necessary_conditions.literal_form: g H*_{t*} - V*_{t*}^2 > 2 alpha and H*_{t*} < H_max/2 on [0,L], with alpha and H_max independent of t* in [0,inf); later g H_1 - V_1^2 > alpha and H_1 < H_max on [0,inf) x [0,L]
necessary_conditions.role: Uniformstrictfluvialmargin and depth bound supply characteristic sign/hyperbolicity and uniform controls. Preserve source constants without deriving or certifying a new numerical lower bound for lambda1/lambda2.
necessary_conditions.producer_original_role: Gives lambda_1 = V_1 + sqrt(g H_1) > 0 > -lambda_2, strict hyperbolicity, and two-sided bounds alpha < lambda_2 < sqrt(g H_max), alpha < lambda_1 < 2 sqrt(g H_max). The entropy construction depends on it. Not to be weakened to H_1 > 0.

necessary_conditions.condition: Friction k nonnegative but arbitrary; slope C in C^2([0,L]); channel length L arbitrary
necessary_conditions.literal_form: k >= 0 arbitrary; C(x) := -g dB/dx with C in C^2([0,L]); no restriction on L
necessary_conditions.role: Explicitly not a small-friction, small-slope or bounded-length result. Do not add such smallness to any candidate or to the old record.

necessary_conditions.condition: Single boundary PI control at x = L through the gate model U = v_G (H(t,L) - U_1(t))
necessary_conditions.source_lines: 198-203 (label vG), 361-369 (label defu1), 372-377 (label boundary2), 380-394 (labels defu12 and boundary1)
necessary_conditions.literal_form: U_1 = k_p (H_c - H(t,L)) + k_I Z with dot Z = H_c - H(t,L) (label Z), giving the static boundary law label boundary2; for a moving target an added feedforward -f(t) with f := H_1 V_1 (t,L)/v_G, giving labels defu12 and boundary1. Z is then redefined as Z - k_p/k_I at line 394 and still satisfies label Z.
necessary_conditions.role: The static control (label boundary2) goes with Corollary 1.8 and Theorem 1.11; the feedforward control (label boundary1) goes with Theorem 1.7. Do not present the feedforward version as usable with only H_c known.

necessary_conditions.condition: Two gain alternatives, kept in their two-branch form
necessary_conditions.source_lines: 470-476 (label cond, in Theorem 1.7) and 486-491 (label cond1, in Corollary 1.8)
necessary_conditions.literal_form: (i) k_p > -1 and k_I > 0; or (ii) k_p < -1 - (g H_1(t,L) - V_1^2(t,L))/(v_G V_1(t,L)) and k_I < 0; in the static case the same with H*(L), V*(L) replacing H_1(t,L), V_1(t,L)
necessary_conditions.role: Keep both gain branches and fixed designed constants; in dynamicTheorem1.7 the second-branch bound depends on the target at all relevanttimes, not onlyinitialtime. Do not turn constant gains into time-varyinggainfunctions.
necessary_conditions.producer_original_role: The second branch involves the sign of V_1(t,L); the gain is not a fixed number but a bound depending on the target at the boundary. Neither branch may be dropped, sign-flipped or merged into 'k_p > -1, k_I > 0'.

necessary_conditions.condition: Unit gate coefficient v_G, as used in the old 2110 title
necessary_conditions.literal_form: v_G appears explicitly in both gain conditions and in the boundary derivatives k_1, k_3; no numerical value is imposed by the theorem
necessary_conditions.role: The old 2110 title says 'unit gate coefficient'. The native text keeps v_G symbolic. This is a scope point to preserve, not a discrepancy to fix.

necessary_conditions.condition: Smallness of the time variation of the inflow, at different orders in different results
necessary_conditions.source_lines: 312-314 (C^2, Prop 1.1), 467 (C^3, Thm 1.7), 555 (C^2, Thm 1.11), 803 (C^3, Lemma 2.4), 840 and 903 (the shrunken hypothesis on d_t H_1 and d_t V_1)
necessary_conditions.literal_form: Prop 1.1: norm of d_t Q_0 in C^2 <= delta. Thm 1.7: norm of d_t Q_0 in C^3 <= delta. Thm 1.11: C^2. Lemma 2.4: C^3. Sections 3 and G work with max(norm of d_t H_1, norm of d_t V_1) in C^1([t0,inf);C^0) < delta.
necessary_conditions.role: The C^k order is part of each statement and is not interchangeable. Lemma 2.4 is what transfers the C^3 bound on Q_0 into the C^1-in-time bound on H_1 and V_1 used in the Lyapunov step. Do not uniformize to 'small d_t Q_0'.

quantifiers_and_regularity.literal_scope: Theorem1.3 assumes the reference target(H1,V1) in C0_tH3_x, but perturbationinitialdata inH2 plusZ0andcompat. Remark1.4addsH3initialdata forH3propagation. Sections3/G use intermediateH3then density. Prop1.1/Thm1.11 eachretain their literalinitialdatastatements and do not automatically inherit allPIconditions.
quantifiers_and_regularity.note: The H^3 assumption is an intermediate technical step of the author's proof, not part of the final statement of Theorem 1.7. Keep both levels distinct.
quantifiers_and_regularity.producer_original_literal_scope: H^2((0,L);R^2) perturbations of (H*,V*) or of (H_1(t0),V_1(t0)), plus |Z^0|, bounded by nu; Theorem 1.3 also asks for H^3 regularity and Remark 1.4 propagates it; Sections 3 and G assume H^3 data and then relax by density (line 901).

quantifiers_and_regularity.literal_scope: Four first-order compatibility conditions linking (H^0,V^0,Z^0), Q_0(0), the derivative of Q_0 at 0, and the time derivative of H_1 V_1 at (0,L); required by Theorem 1.3 and by Definition 1.5.
quantifiers_and_regularity.note: The third and fourth lines of that display contain the author's literal expressions; nothing here is corrected or re-derived.

quantifiers_and_regularity.literal_scope: For any T > t0 >= 0 and any admissible data, the solution exists on [t0,T] and the decay holds for all t in [t0,T] with constants C and gamma independent of t0 and T; nu in Definition 1.5 is uniform, and Remark 2.3 is what removes the (T-t0) dependence introduced by Lemma 2.2.
quantifiers_and_regularity.note: Uniformity in t0 and T is part of the claimed content.

quantifiers_and_regularity.literal_scope: A convolution of |d_t Q_0| + |d2_tt Q_0| + |d3_ttt Q_0| with an exponential weight, divided by the decay factor: exponent mu/2 in Proposition 1.1, exponent gamma in Theorem 1.11.
quantifiers_and_regularity.note: Three time derivatives of Q_0 appear inside the integral; the weight exponent differs between the two statements as printed.

quantifiers_and_regularity.literal_scope: Definition1.5exponentialstability measuresH2 pairerror plus|Z|. Prop1.1free-targetISSandThm1.11staticPI-ISS display only pairH2error;do not append|Z|to their author conclusions.
quantifiers_and_regularity.note: As recorded in the old 2110 judgment, H^2 here is a Sobolev norm, not an H2 difficulty grade.
quantifiers_and_regularity.producer_original_literal_scope: The stability norm is the H^2 Sobolev norm on (0,L) for the pair (H - H_1, V - V_1), plus |Z|.
